  - [ARG-047](../record/arguments.d/ARG-047.md) — Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy's "agency is a matter of perspective" supports the claim that perspectival, agential and institutional boundaries need not coincide *(Rejected, source)*
  - [ARG-048](../record/arguments.d/ARG-048.md) — Tsoukas and Chia's radial extension and institutionalization show how the exercise of a shared perspective can transform it with no agent governing the change, the agents and the institution kept distinct *(Proposed, source)*
- [CLAIM-430](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-430.md) — An interaction can make available a way of relating that its participants' operative perspectives did not hold, by giving each a role to enact in it, so that taking part can come before, and help produce, the reinterpretation it later seems to express; whether the change stays with the partner, generalizes to a category, or is reproduced beyond the encounter are further questions *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-044](../record/arguments.d/ARG-044.md) — The MSF meeting reanalysed by Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy shows that an interaction can make available a way of relating its participants did not hold, and names the condition under which it lasts; it does not show that taking part comes before the reinterpretation *(Proposed, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-448](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-448.md) — An ordinal potential describes only the winning-move relation it is computed on; where an organization's legibility regime selects which contests are admitted or recorded, an acyclic record, even a persistent potential, can be the product of selective contestation, so observed coherence is not evidence that the organization's perspectives are integrated, and an intervention that improves its self-governance may at first increase the disagreement observed *(Active, counter)*
  - [ARG-066](../record/arguments.d/ARG-066.md) — A three-perspective majority cycle, with a chair who admits only two of its three contests, gives a coherent record of perspectives that are not integrated, and so shows that coherence produced by selective contestation can exist; it does not show that it persists or what real interventions do *(Proposed, existence)*
  - [ARG-073](../record/arguments.d/ARG-073.md) — The DeGroot–Friedkin result, in which every issue ends in consensus while members not every other member listens to, even indirectly, end with no power, shows that a coherent record can coexist with excluded members, not that a maintained regime admitting some contests produces the coherence *(Proposed, existence)*
- [CLAIM-478](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md) — Rate differences help make structure and not only mark it: where some degrees of freedom settle faster than others by more than the rates vary among them, the relation they settle into is a constraint on the system over the window between the two rates, so what is a realization at one rate works as a constraint at another; and organization can make new rate differences in turn, as when modes slow near an instability and become order parameters, so hierarchies of rates and constraints can produce one another *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-125](../record/arguments.d/ARG-125.md) — Simon's near-decomposability, read through a finite correlation length, shows that a system off criticality divides into approximately autonomous levels of description *(Rejected, source)*
- [CLAIM-484](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-484.md) — Internal conflict is the gap between the precedence a motive claims over action and the authority the rest of the organization grants it *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-049](../record/arguments.d/ARG-049.md) — The pauses, averted gaze and reversal in the MSF transcript show internal conflict as a gap between the precedence a motive claims and the authority it is granted *(Rejected, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-486](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-486.md) — A rendering can keep the communicative act while changing the proposition, so preserving the proposition is not necessary for preserving the communicative event *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-020](../record/arguments.d/ARG-020.md) — The compensation hypothesis gives the mechanism by which a rendering keeps the act while changing the proposition *(Rejected, cause-to-effect)*
  - [ARG-021](../record/arguments.d/ARG-021.md) — The manuscript's renderings, which keep the words and change the act, show that keeping the proposition is not necessary for keeping the act *(Rejected, existence)*
- [CLAIM-491](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-491.md) — No action is selfless in the sense of aiming at a good that is no self's: what is called selflessness, collectivist or altruistic, is concern for the good of a self extended to include others or a group, so collectivism is self-interest on a larger self-identity *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-076](../record/arguments.d/ARG-076.md) — Eyerman's cultural trauma and Volkan's chosen trauma are evidence for the owner's thesis only for chosen trauma, where an ancestral injury is taken up as an injury to a present group identity and felt as grievance when that identity is threatened; they do not tell an enlarged self from a switched one, and they leave mourning for particular dead open *(Proposed, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-497](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-497.md) — A system's causes are found at the coarsest description whose interventions are unambiguous: a macro description is causally proportionate where it merges only micro states that intervention cannot tell apart, and no coarse-graining carries more causal information than the micro description it supervenes on *(Active, thesis)*
  - [ARG-041](../record/arguments.d/ARG-041.md) — From the effective-information bound and its ties to proportionality: a gain that depends on the intervention distribution is not a property of the system, the coarse-grainings that lose nothing are, and the coarsest of them is where the causes are *(Proposed, formal-application)*
- [CLAIM-511](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-511.md) — A self-maintaining organization ought to preserve its corrigibility *(Proposed, disclaimed)*
  - [ARG-042](../record/arguments.d/ARG-042.md) — Studies and constructions of how an organization keeps its capacity for correction show that self-maintaining organizations ought to preserve their corrigibility *(Rejected, evidence)*
    - [CLAIM-520](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-520.md) — The value of keeping a corrective capacity is conditional on objectives, uncertainty and cost: a free, optional audit cannot lower a single time-consistent decision-maker's expected performance, but an audit that costs C to maintain and bears on k decisions with error rate ε is worth k(0.25 − 0.5ε) − C in the exchange's model, negative when C is large or k small, and where no hypothesis fits the world, correction gains no reward and improves only calibration *(Active, thesis)*
- [CLAIM-518](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-518.md) — Normative judgments about an organization's continuity, reform or obligations can depend on diachronic relations that descriptions of present states or terminal outcomes do not show, so specifying the relevant relations and histories can be necessary to apply them adequately; which continuations ought to follow is a further normative question, not a prerequisite of every normative judgment *(Active, thesis)*
  - [ARG-043](../record/arguments.d/ARG-043.md) — Bencherki's checklist and daycare, one end state with opposite verdicts, show a normative judgment about an organization that depends on a history its end state does not show *(Proposed, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-521](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-521.md) — An organization's present coupling strength need not reveal the stability of the process maintaining it: in a constructed system whose maintained connector and capacities set a three-unit coupling, the recovery rate of the maintenance goes to zero at its saddle-node while the coupling's spectral gap there stays near 0.989 *(Active, thesis)*
  - [ARG-068](../record/arguments.d/ARG-068.md) — A coordination mode held stable by a capacity declining from below its maintenance threshold is an instance of the dissociation between a coupling's strength and the stability of the saddle-node maintaining it *(Rejected, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-522](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-522.md) — Recovery under interventions on state cannot show where maintenance is realized: an outside controller that measures the constraint capacities and supplies the internal production law as state feedback yields the same trajectory under every perturbation of state, damage and recovery included, even with every capacity observed exactly; only interventions on the production mechanisms, relative to a declared boundary, separate the two *(Active, thesis)*
  - [ARG-050](../record/arguments.d/ARG-050.md) — An intervention that disables a production pathway inside a declared boundary, or interrupts an outside controller, locates the producer of a maintained organization, because the pathway causes the capacities with a delay and can be intervened on surgically, so the fat-handedness of interventions on wholes does not reach the inference *(Active, contrast)*
- [CLAIM-532](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-532.md) — An unresolved discrepancy is an occasion for self-formation, the transformation dimension of a will-organization, and not a guarantee of it; it suffices for self-formation that the agent's own activity on such a discrepancy produce a maintained capacity, either a new distinction, its policy coming to depend on a feature of its situation it did not depend on, or a new channel, the outcomes it can reach under its own policy growing, that outlasts the discrepancy and serves a class of later ones, as shown by transfer to discrepancies of the same class after the inducing conditions are gone and by interventions on the processes that produce the capacity while it forms *(Active, thesis)*
  - [ARG-060](../record/arguments.d/ARG-060.md) — Three organizations failing one task for three different reasons show that a new distinction and a new channel of action are separate repairs, and that a new action stands in for a missing distinction only where some action is acceptable in every circumstance the organization cannot tell apart *(Proposed, contrast)*
- [CLAIM-547](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-547.md) — Cooperation within groups and the coexistence of groups are distinct targets that can trade off: in the group-selection rule of Nowak's five, b/c > 1 + n/m, cooperation spreads because a group that grows to size n splits and another group is driven extinct, so the mechanism that stabilizes cooperation inside groups works by removing groups; cooperation local to a group, the persistence of several groups whose interests are opposed, and concern for those outside one's group are three achievements, and none of them secures the next *(Active, thesis)*
  - [ARG-052](../record/arguments.d/ARG-052.md) — Van Lange and Bergmann's model of intergroup cooperation shows that cooperation within groups and the coexistence of groups are distinct targets that can trade off *(Rejected, source)*
- [CLAIM-558](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md) — A procedural capability that operation seldom calls on decays with the time since its last use, and practice in the interval slows the decay, so a capability kept for rare events is maintained by practice outside operation, not by operation *(Active, thesis)*
  - [ARG-201](../record/arguments.d/ARG-201.md) — From the task-type split of Tatel's meta-analysis, whose medical and dental tasks still lose accuracy with disuse at about half the pooled rate, the disuse premise of the claim on capabilities kept for rare events holds for real-world procedures at a lower and decelerating rate, which qualifies the claim and does not defeat it *(Proposed, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-571](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-571.md) — For a fixed architecture and one resource that must be held at each moment, the resource threshold for reaching a target configuration need not equal the resource requirement of the target: it is the least, over admissible transition paths, of the peak requirement along the path, and it is infinite when no admissible path joins the two *(Active, thesis)*
  - [ARG-077](../record/arguments.d/ARG-077.md) — The barrier at 1.3 between two configurations that each cost 0.7 shows that the threshold for reaching a configuration need not equal its requirement *(Active, existence)*
- [CLAIM-584](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-584.md) — Maintaining a specialized capability that is seldom or never exercised for its specialized function is wasteful *(Proposed, disclaimed)*
  - [ARG-053](../record/arguments.d/ARG-053.md) — Constructed rescue squads kept at a cost and seldom or never exercised are evidence, by their low observed exercise, that a specialized capability's maintenance expenditure is wasteful *(Rejected, evidence)*
    - [CLAIM-561](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-561.md) — When early activation reduces intervention delay under uncertainty, provisionally mobilizing a specialized resource can minimize expected loss even when the resource is more likely to be canceled than used; a cancellation rate alone therefore cannot identify waste *(Active, thesis)*
- [CLAIM-588](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-588.md) — Relieving an incompatibility, redistributing an unavoidable mismatch and exploiting a mismatch dynamically are three design targets, which change respectively the compatibility complex, where residuals or loads concentrate, and stability, barriers or transition paths, and the last two can be achieved without the first *(Active, thesis)*
  - [ARG-054](../record/arguments.d/ARG-054.md) — Rocks and Mehta's prestress, placed on different bonds of a self-stress space fixed by geometry, changes which force excites a zero mode and retunes stability while the zero modes and self-stresses stay fixed, and so gives a mechanical parallel to redistributing and exploiting a mismatch without relief, though it shows the exciting force moving and not a given load *(Active, analogy)*
- [CLAIM-606](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md) — A localized structure can persist by an internal balance that needs no supply, by a balance of gain and loss that needs a standing supply, or by a topological charge that continuous change cannot remove, and the three differ in what carries the structure's identity, how it forms and how it ends; because thresholds and abrupt ends appear in all of them, even with no supply at all, only withdrawing the supply and measuring the outflow tells which route a structure is on *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-111](../record/arguments.d/ARG-111.md) — The charge sectors of topological solitons carry the topological route to persistence as the protection of a kind and its net count, not as the identity of a particular soliton: a translated kink and a winding-two vortex sector keep the charge while the token changes *(Proposed, formal-application)*
- [CLAIM-612](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-612.md) — Statistics conditioned on survival can be stationary and quickly reached while absorption is certain: in a finite chain whose viable states all lead to an absorbing failure, the distribution of the survivors settles on the mixing time and the survivors die out on a time longer by the ratio of the spectral gap to the hazard, so a surviving organization's stable statistics are no evidence that it persists *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-056](../record/arguments.d/ARG-056.md) — A three-state chain whose survivors settle in a few time units while all of them die out on a time a hundred times longer shows that stable statistics conditioned on survival come apart from persistence *(Proposed, existence)*
- [CLAIM-613](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-613.md) — A fork can be the construction of a new organization through which a disposition that the parent's governance kept ineffective gains efficacy, and not only one of several successors of the parent *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-069](../record/arguments.d/ARG-069.md) — Hirschman's exit and voice, in which members denied effective voice can still exit, carries over to a fork as the construction of a new organization through which a disposition the parent kept ineffective gains efficacy *(Proposed, analogy)*
- [CLAIM-615](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-615.md) — An organized individual's identity over time is carried by the causal transmission of the relations that keep its repertoire realizable, not by its constituents or by any structure invariant across its realizations, so a structuralism about individuals has to be historical: the structure can change under maps that are not isomorphisms while the individual continues, two structurally identical copies can be two individuals, the transmitting organization may lie outside the individual, and when those relations part at a succession, different successors can continue different respects of it *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-075](../record/arguments.d/ARG-075.md) — Two separately made mechanisms of one design are isomorphic and two, and a mechanism can be stipulated to persist through a change that breaks isomorphism; the first carries over to organized individuals and the second only as consistency, so whether such an individual continues needs a criterion of continuation *(Proposed, analogy)*
- [CLAIM-616](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-616.md) — Synchronization phenomena can serve as a laboratory for the record's organizational distinctions: locking regions for compatibility, external forcing for support and dependence, the driven and suppressed oscillator for autonomy against coercion, and entrainment and phase locking for individuation transitions; a drive fixes where control lies, not whether it is legitimate *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-072](../record/arguments.d/ARG-072.md) — Synchronization phenomena, used as model systems, can separate the record's distinctions of compatibility, dependence and suppression, because a driven and suppressed oscillator and a coupled pair with a relative phase separate them by intervention, though a drive fixes where control lies and not whether it is coercive *(Proposed, analogy)*
- [CLAIM-617](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-617.md) — When a project's continuities part at a change of steward, participants' judgements of which successor continues it are causally productive of that succession: those who judge one successor illegitimate move their work to another, and the move transfers the productive organization the judgement was about *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-067](../record/arguments.d/ARG-067.md) — Contested open-source successions, in which participants who judged a new steward illegitimate moved their work to another successor, are evidence that the participants' verdicts help make the succession *(Proposed, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-618](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-618.md) — Indexed by a system's control parameters, the compatibility complex of its synchronization demands gives each set of demands a region where they can be met together; an Arnold tongue is a locking region, where a demand is met by an attracting state, and each locking region lies inside the compatibility region of the same demands without needing to equal it *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-061](../record/arguments.d/ARG-061.md) — The inclusion of a locking region in the compatibility region of the same demands follows from the phase-oscillator setting once a demand is an acceptance set of phase differences and the admissible configurations are the locked ones *(Proposed, formal-application)*
- [CLAIM-619](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-619.md) — An organization can be disposed to answer a credible challenge by reducing the capacity for future challenge, classifying the challenge as the problem and restricting the challenger, so that the later absence of challenges reads as success; the test is whether a credible challenge causally lowers the chance of effective future challenge against a control, and the test alone does not say whether the response finks the disposition to be corrected, masks it, or changes only the challengers' access and incentives *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-059](../record/arguments.d/ARG-059.md) — A label that produces the conduct confirming it carries over to a response to challenge that produces the absence of challenge confirming it, though one loop runs through the labelled person's conduct and the other through the challenger's access *(Proposed, analogy)*
  - [ARG-070](../record/arguments.d/ARG-070.md) — Pohlhaus's willful hermeneutical ignorance, unread here, is offered as what normative inversion resembles, and the record cannot yet check the resemblance *(Deferred, source)*
- [CLAIM-623](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-623.md) — Forgetting a hidden mechanism can turn a sheaf of histories into a presheaf of realizable observations that is not a sheaf: when the union of two overlapping intervals is itself an observable context, two observed histories can each be realizable and agree on their overlap with no realization of their union, so a gluing failure need not show a disagreement on an overlap or a cycle of three contexts *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-074](../record/arguments.d/ARG-074.md) — A hidden mode fixed for a run, whose observations over two overlapping periods agree on the overlap and do not paste into a realizable history, shows that a presheaf of realizable observations can fail to glue *(Proposed, existence)*
- [CLAIM-624](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-624.md) — The wrong beyond violation that an organization commits by reproducing representations and allocations of authority that keep a justified standard from constraining it is a breach of a second-order duty of answerability: to maintain feasible means for relevant violations to become knowable, contestable and correctable; it is a verdict only given an independently justified standard and a feasible alternative *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-055](../record/arguments.d/ARG-055.md) — A matched-harm construction, in which two institutions under a stipulated duty to maintain independent review cause the same harm and reach the same remedy but differ in keeping that duty and in reproducing its breach, shows that a second-order wrong of answerability can come apart from the first-order harm and its continuation *(Proposed, existence)*
  - [ARG-058](../record/arguments.d/ARG-058.md) — If the second-order duty of answerability were unconditional it would entail that a self-maintaining organization ought to preserve its corrigibility, which the record disclaims, so the duty must be bounded by obligation, capability and reasonable alternatives *(Proposed, reductio)*
  - [ARG-062](../record/arguments.d/ARG-062.md) — The Challenger-to-Columbia history is evidence that an organization can reproduce the conditions that keep a known hazard from constraining it, reforms undone included, though it says nothing of a second-order wrong *(Proposed, evidence)*
  - [ARG-063](../record/arguments.d/ARG-063.md) — A two-regime reporting construction shows that a harmful outcome and the regime that keeps it unrecorded can sustain each other without intent, separating actual from recorded violation, and shows nothing normative *(Proposed, existence)*
  - [ARG-064](../record/arguments.d/ARG-064.md) — A self-maintaining protective regime, whose interventions shift the evidence and authority that judge it, carries over to a harm-producing organization once a normative predicate replaces the evidence of continued need: the reproductive mechanism transfers and the verdict does not *(Proposed, analogy)*
  - [ARG-071](../record/arguments.d/ARG-071.md) — The Wells Fargo directors' report shows a performance regime reproducing its narrow construal of harm through its own success *(Rejected, evidence)*
  - [ARG-114](../record/arguments.d/ARG-114.md) — Given a means-end principle of responsibility, an authority that owes a duty whose fulfilment needs a capability it is responsible for and can maintain at justified cost owes the maintenance of an adequate one, absent a defeater: a conditional derivation of the second-order duty of answerability, valid with the principle as a premise, in which the responsibility condition does the work of feasibility and the reflexive condition constrains what counts as adequate *(Proposed, formal-application)*
- [CLAIM-627](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-627.md) — Whether a contested concept's uses are compatible is partly settled by who has jurisdiction over its contexts: which contexts count as relevant to a decision and which rule governs where they overlap fix part of the cover on which its uses must glue, so a will-organization's jurisdiction and precedence act on the conditions of interpretation and not only on its outputs *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-057](../record/arguments.d/ARG-057.md) — A rule whose outcomes change when classification moves to another group, with the rule unchanged, is evidence that jurisdiction over a concept's contexts partly fixes whether its uses are compatible *(Rejected, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-646](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-646.md) — Peak-capacity thresholds do not fix cumulative transition costs: two systems can have the same threshold between every pair of configurations, and so the same hierarchy of budgeted classes, while the least cumulative cost of a transition differs between them by any factor *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-078](../record/arguments.d/ARG-078.md) — The chain and the complete graph on the same configurations show that peak-capacity thresholds do not fix cumulative transition costs *(Proposed, existence)*
- [CLAIM-647](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-647.md) — Replacing the base model a specialization was learned into can impose a compatibility or transfer cost that shortens the specialization's useful life, though nothing it encodes has become false: in the trade between learning once and computing on demand, the reader's turnover is a staleness term of its own, beside the world's changing; how often the cost binds, and whether it tips the trade toward computing on demand, is empirical *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-079](../record/arguments.d/ARG-079.md) — Because a LoRA module is an additive update to one set of frozen pretrained weights, amplifying directions already in them, replacing those weights leaves the module without the base it was defined on, so its effect on the new base is not guaranteed and has to be re-established, by transfer or by retraining *(Proposed, cause-to-effect)*
  - [ARG-080](../record/arguments.d/ARG-080.md) — IP-Adapter's statement that fine-tuned image-prompt models are "not compatible with other base models" shows that a trained specialization goes stale when its base model is replaced *(Rejected, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-648](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-648.md) — On Bickhard's account the owner's debugging case has an endogenous form: a self-maintaining system that anticipates an interaction will sustain it holds an expected response profile set by its own upkeep, the absence or shortfall of the response means by its own lights that the interaction failed, and that norm and a designer's profile come apart where the system's persistence is at stake *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-083](../record/arguments.d/ARG-083.md) — Bickhard's account and the two-profile forager show that a profile set by a system's own upkeep is a norm different from a designer's, with the same silent case and different verdicts where persistence is at stake *(Proposed, existence)*
- [CLAIM-649](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-649.md) — An absence of response under an inserted intervention with an expected response profile is diagnostic evidence about the mechanism under test, carried with nothing emitted: under a probabilistic response model it shifts support toward fault by its likelihood ratio, and in the limiting case of a deterministic, independently validated response guarantee it entails that the guarantee was violated *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-084](../record/arguments.d/ARG-084.md) — Under a deterministic, independently validated response guarantee, an absence of the guaranteed response to a delivered intervention entails that the guarantee was violated *(Proposed, formal-application)*
  - [ARG-085](../record/arguments.d/ARG-085.md) — From the debugger's test and a probabilistic response model to the defeasible reading: an absence under an intervention with an expected response shifts support toward fault by its likelihood ratio *(Proposed, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-650](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-650.md) — Grice's factivity test shows that a designed alarm's content can be false: its sounding means, factively, that the detector crossed its threshold, and carries "fire" only as a non-factive content, so a false alarm's error lies there; what makes "fire" the content it is supposed to carry is a separate question, answered for this designed alarm by its designer's intention and left open, between selection history and organizational maintenance, for other systems *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-081](../record/arguments.d/ARG-081.md) — Because a false alarm's error lies in a non-factive content, Grice's analysis shows that the norm that content answers to is an intention, the designer's *(Rejected, formal-application)*
  - [ARG-082](../record/arguments.d/ARG-082.md) — Grice's factivity test, applied to the steam alarm, places the false alarm's error in a non-factive content *(Proposed, formal-application)*
  - [ARG-204](../record/arguments.d/ARG-204.md) — Millikan's biosemantics, read beside the SEP survey, independently corroborates that a false alarm's error cannot lie in its natural meaning, and qualifies the separation of where the error lies from what fixes the norm *(Proposed, source)*
- [CLAIM-652](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-652.md) — An organization that weighs a harmful practice by the failures its present users report can expand the practice with no act against complaint: as the harmed leave, the recognized cost of the practice falls with their share, so the score favours more of it, and the failures it records grow more slowly than the harm it does *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-092](../record/arguments.d/ARG-092.md) — The exit-driven drift toy shows that a practice can expand under an honest count of present users' complaints, through the exit it causes alone *(Proposed, existence)*
- [CLAIM-653](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-653.md) — Where a content industry reads demand from activity or revenue, the minority of heaviest users comes to set the distribution of content everyone is offered; and if heavy users habituate and seek more extreme material, the mainstream drifts toward it, which may explain why mainstream pornography channels now carry material once niche or extreme *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-089](../record/arguments.d/ARG-089.md) — The works read on 2026-11-12 support only the premise that platforms reading demand from activity shape what is produced; they do not show the heaviest users setting what everyone is offered, and they leave the escalation half unsupported *(Proposed, evidence)*
  - [ARG-095](../record/arguments.d/ARG-095.md) — The survey and audit evidence A reports supports the structural half of the heavy-user mechanism in pornography distribution only as possible, and does not support the escalation half: the associations are small, observational and self-reported, and the one longitudinal content study runs against it *(Proposed, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-654](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-654.md) — Reachability by a given process grows with the budget when the process's choices do not depend on how much budget remains and success means reaching the target within the budget; a process whose choices depend on the remaining budget can reach a target at a small budget and miss it at a larger one, though the admissible-path reachability of the same architecture grows with the budget *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-086](../record/arguments.d/ARG-086.md) — The trap construction shows that reachability by a budget-dependent process can fall as the budget rises while path reachability does not *(Proposed, existence)*
- [CLAIM-656](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-656.md) — The selection that lets economically weighted demand set a product's design extends to news: where attention is the revenue, optimizing for it favours clickbait and works against investigative journalism, whose findings cannot be shown to be in demand before they exist and whose value falls largely to people who never pay for them *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-088](../record/arguments.d/ARG-088.md) — The works read on 2026-11-12 support the news claim's externality step and, narrowly, its selection for attention in wording, but not its central step that attention optimization costs investigative capacity; the readings it cited as grounds carry less than it cited them for *(Proposed, evidence)*
  - [ARG-091](../record/arguments.d/ARG-091.md) — The selection mechanism shown for loot-box economies transfers to news in its structure, demand read through an economic weight shapes supply, and does not transfer in what it weights or in what it predicts, since news is weighted by attention and an investigation's value is largely external and cannot be shown before it is found *(Proposed, analogy)*
- [CLAIM-659](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-659.md) — Microchimerism, cells of mother and offspring persisting in each other for decades and some of them taking part in the host's regulation, bears on the view that biological individuality is graded or processual: the separation that gestation begins is not completed at birth at the level of cells *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-090](../record/arguments.d/ARG-090.md) — The persistence of maternal microchimeric cells, and the dependence of offspring tolerance on one marked subset of them, are evidence that the separation of mother and offspring is incomplete at the level of cells, and not by themselves evidence that individuality is graded *(Proposed, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-660](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-660.md) — Behaviour-manipulating parasites show one organism's selected adaptations controlling another's behaviour through the host's own machinery, not goals the parasite represents and imposes: evolutionary goal-directedness and causal control come apart from intentional agency, and that an action is executed by the host's own mechanisms does not show that the host's governance of it is independent *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-087](../record/arguments.d/ARG-087.md) — The parasite cases, with manipulation stronger in mature parasite stages and in the presence of the right predator, are evidence that the hosts' behaviour is controlled by the parasites' selected adaptations; they are no evidence for or against the parasites' representing goals *(Proposed, evidence)*
  - [ARG-094](../record/arguments.d/ARG-094.md) — Pathogen-specific changes in host behaviour do not by themselves show manipulation, since sterile immune challenges produce them through the host's own sickness programmes; what does tell selected parasite adaptation from host response is dependence on the parasite's stage, which trophically transmitted helminths show *(Proposed, contrast)*
- [CLAIM-663](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-663.md) — The distinctions of the PASS@(k,T) analysis are the record's distinctions of resource-bounded realization: its capability boundary is reachability by a given process under a budget, its efficiency is reliable attainment, and its interaction depth is a resource index, so whether an intervention expands what an organization can do or only makes it more reliable is the record's question of reachable against reliably reached *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-093](../record/arguments.d/ARG-093.md) — PASS@(k,T)'s capability boundary, efficiency and interaction depth correspond to the record's reachability by a process, reliable attainment and resource index, with two differences: the paper's process is a stochastic policy that can change with its budget, and its success is judged by an oracle *(Proposed, analogy)*
- [CLAIM-666](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-666.md) — A migration of the record's grammar is faithful when it preserves the record's accountability structure, not its old graph: where the old grammar forced a relation nobody asserted, a faithful migration removes it *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-096](../record/arguments.d/ARG-096.md) — The graph that asserted an inference nobody made shows that preserving the old graph through a migration can preserve a false dependency *(Proposed, existence)*
- [CLAIM-667](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-667.md) — Governance raises the value of a modifiable schema on tasks whose inherited categories are inadequate: with review, rationale and migration, letting a collective change its schema improves justified correction more than it does without them *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-098](../record/arguments.d/ARG-098.md) — EvoOntology's gate ablation shows that governance raises the value of a modifiable schema *(Rejected, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-668](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-668.md) — A shared record can represent who contributed a proposition and what standing the record gives it, but not what any collaborator believes or that all of them know the current standing: access to the record is a precondition of coordinating on it, not evidence that they have *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-097](../record/arguments.d/ARG-097.md) — Halpern and Moses's result on unreliable channels applies to a record read asynchronously: publishing a standing does not make it common knowledge *(Proposed, formal-application)*
- [CLAIM-669](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-669.md) — An arrangement can exploit through the access it grants: a needed good offered on terms that leave the recipient with a lasting encumbrance, a reliance on the provider or an obligation hard to escape, that narrows later exit or renegotiation, so that exploitation can arise through inclusion that succeeds, not only through inclusion that fails, and widening access need not reduce it *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-100](../record/arguments.d/ARG-100.md) — Seamster and Charron-Chénier's predatory inclusion in education debt shows that an arrangement can exploit through the access it grants, and that widening access need not reduce it *(Proposed, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-671](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-671.md) — Where an organizational transformation increases a constituent's vulnerability to the discretionary choices of a responsible agent, and that vulnerability grounds special obligations under an independently justified principle, the transformation can strengthen that agent's responsibilities toward the constituent *(Proposed, supposed)*
  - [ARG-099](../record/arguments.d/ARG-099.md) — Fineman's vulnerability account shows that an organizational transformation that increases constituents' vulnerability to a responsible agent's discretion strengthens that agent's responsibilities toward them *(Rejected, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-672](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-672.md) — How a form is kept in being is not fixed by the form: the same still form can persist as a fixed point, by repairing itself after a strike, or by being rebuilt by a larger pattern it serves, and taking on a constitutive role can change which of these holds, so a form's stabilization and its role, though they can come apart, are not independent *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-101](../record/arguments.d/ARG-101.md) — A still life that is a fixed point alone and is broken and rebuilt in a role, by itself or by the pattern it serves, shows that the mechanism keeping a form in being can change with the form's role *(Proposed, existence)*
- [CLAIM-674](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-674.md) — An arrangement, a technology among them, can satisfy people's preferences more fully, and raise the well-being they report, while narrowing their opportunities to engage actively with what is worthwhile, so success at satisfying preferences does not show that the lives an arrangement leaves open are going better *(Active, thesis)*
  - [ARG-102](../record/arguments.d/ARG-102.md) — Marcuse's false needs and Illich's needs that productivity cannot satisfy corroborate the claim that satisfying preferences more fully need not leave lives going better, but by criteria the claim does not adopt, Marcuse's origin in particular interests and Illich's level of conviviality, so they support its separation of satisfaction from how lives go, not a measure of worth *(Proposed, source)*
  - [ARG-106](../record/arguments.d/ARG-106.md) — Wolf's Tanner Lectures carry the premise of three of the flourishing claims, that fulfilment and meaning come apart, that no one in particular has authority over worth, and that meaning pursued for its own sake defeats itself, but not their application to arrangements and institutions, which Wolf disclaims and which is A's *(Proposed, source)*
- [CLAIM-675](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md) — Two forms of support that give a party the same capabilities now can leave it different capabilities later: where capacity is learned by doing and decays with disuse, support that does the work shrinks what the party can reach unaided while support that covers only its shortfall does not, so support, or a technology, cannot be ranked by present capability sets and has to be assessed by the capability trajectory it produces *(Active, thesis)*
  - [ARG-105](../record/arguments.d/ARG-105.md) — Gardner's objection that Sen gives no argument for preferring capability to achievement qualifies the framing of the claim that support must be assessed by the capability trajectory it produces, and leaves its derivation standing, which holds for achieved functionings as well *(Proposed, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-677](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md) — A technology can become practically compulsory without any rule requiring it: as infrastructures, competitors and expectations adapt to its adoption, the alternatives left to those who decline it shrink, so the freedom an arrangement leaves is measured by what remains open to a non-adopter, not by what it lets adopters do *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-104](../record/arguments.d/ARG-104.md) — Arthur's increasing-returns lock-in carries to the claim that a technology can become practically compulsory for those who decline it only for the infrastructural mechanism, and only where non-adoption is a third option whose returns fall as adoptions accumulate *(Proposed, analogy)*
  - [ARG-107](../record/arguments.d/ARG-107.md) — Energy and Equity supports the compulsion claim's mechanism and measure with the shoe and school cases, the non-adopter barred without any intentional conspiracy, but qualifies "without any rule requiring it": the technology's adoption needs no rule, while the exclusion of those who decline it can be enforced by gatekeepers and by law *(Proposed, source)*
  - [ARG-108](../record/arguments.d/ARG-108.md) — One-Dimensional Man corroborates the mechanism of practical compulsion, a project that once operative tends to become exclusive and makes compliance rational, but argues against measuring freedom by the options left open, since what can be chosen and what is chosen are shaped as well, an argument of the kind the compulsion claim's second defeater describes *(Proposed, source)*
- [CLAIM-680](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-680.md) — That some ways of living are more worthwhile than others, and that this can be judged fallibly, licenses institutions to cultivate the conditions in which people can engage with what is worthwhile, not to impose a conception of it: a reasoned judgment of worth is not by itself a warrant for coercion *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-106](../record/arguments.d/ARG-106.md) — Wolf's Tanner Lectures carry the premise of three of the flourishing claims, that fulfilment and meaning come apart, that no one in particular has authority over worth, and that meaning pursued for its own sake defeats itself, but not their application to arrangements and institutions, which Wolf disclaims and which is A's *(Proposed, source)*
- [CLAIM-682](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md) — A dependence becomes presumptively dominating by those who control it when three conditions coincide: participation in an important sphere of life rests on the arrangement, those who control it hold consequential discretion over the dependent, and the dependent lacks effective means of protection, influence, challenge or justified withdrawal; this is a test for domination by an arrangement's controllers, not for every unfreedom, and impersonal constraint that no one holds is outside it *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-109](../record/arguments.d/ARG-109.md) — Han's seductive power and auto-exploitation, Benjamin's default discrimination and Marcuse's administration, which runs through the choice of a society's project and is veiled, show that a complete dependence can be domination or unfreedom on serious accounts without anyone holding present discretion over the dependent, so the domination threshold holds only as a test for domination by an arrangement's controllers *(Proposed, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-683](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-683.md) — When an institution makes measured meaningfulness a target that shapes participants' incentives or self-understanding, it can induce proxy optimization or self-conscious meaning-seeking that displaces engagement with worthwhile activities *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-106](../record/arguments.d/ARG-106.md) — Wolf's Tanner Lectures carry the premise of three of the flourishing claims, that fulfilment and meaning come apart, that no one in particular has authority over worth, and that meaning pursued for its own sake defeats itself, but not their application to arrangements and institutions, which Wolf disclaims and which is A's *(Proposed, source)*
- [CLAIM-684](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-684.md) — When a choice about a technology or an institution could substantially and durably narrow the possibilities later open to those it affects, the burden of justifying it should rise with the size and the irreversibility of the narrowing *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-103](../record/arguments.d/ARG-103.md) — Winner's essay supports the premise and the occasion of the irreversibility burden, that the latitude of choice about a technology is greatest at its introduction and vanishes once commitments are made, so that innovations deserve the scrutiny given to laws, but not the rule that the burden of justification scales with the size and irreversibility of the narrowing *(Proposed, source)*
- [CLAIM-690](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-690.md) — Whichever way a whole and its part depend on each other, the same magnitude of dependence can run either way, and what sorts it is who controls the terms on which it is met, exit, renegotiation and the conditions of supply, while the magnitude and the integration that produced it set only how much rides on it: with the part able to withdraw or renegotiate, the whole's need of it becomes the part's hold on its terms; with the terms at an agent's discretion, the same need gives the part none, and the part's own dependence becomes vulnerability to that agent, on whom, under a principle grounding obligations in such vulnerability, the strengthened responsibility falls *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-110](../record/arguments.d/ARG-110.md) — Two workshops equal in dependence, integration and membership and different only in who controls the terms show that control sorts a whole-part dependence in both directions, given that one dependence can be organized more than one way *(Proposed, contrast)*
- [CLAIM-709](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-709.md) — Equality of wrongdoing and equality of power are separate questions: two parties can each act wrongly, even as often, while only one holds control over the terms of the other's life, so a tally of wrongful acts does not settle who is responsible for the relationship's coercive structure, and a finding of that control does not excuse the controlled party's own wrongful acts *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-113](../record/arguments.d/ARG-113.md) — A stipulated couple in which the partner who strikes more often is the one controlled shows that the count of wrongful acts and control over the terms of the relationship can come apart *(Proposed, existence)*
- [CLAIM-712](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-712.md) — Traceability does not settle fair attribution: a record can identify exactly which agent approved an outcome while leaving open whether that agent had the time, information, authority and alternatives that responsibility for it requires, so two arrangements with equally complete audit trails can warrant very different attributions *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-720](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-720.md) — Inalienability is a limit on normative powers, not on exercise: a person may restrict the exercise of a right or delegate limited authority over decisions, and no delegation, contract, collective decision or success in imposing an arrangement thereby confers authority to determine whether that person keeps the standing from which claims against the arrangement arise, because the holder lacks the power to confer it *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-726](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-726.md) — A party can arrange the conditions under which another commits a real wrong and then use the true accusation, before an audience whose judgement it anticipated, to justify further control over them; the truth of the accusation neither vindicates the party that arranged it nor excuses the one who did wrong *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-728](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-728.md) — In an incomplete contract the party holding residual rights of control decides the contingencies the contract did not cover, so a relationship fair in every specified term can still leave one party's terms at the other's discretion, and that discretion is exercised, and seen, only when an uncovered contingency arises *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-751](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-751.md) — The upstream provenance of a failure can be carried without blame: an investigator barred from assigning blame or liability traced the Tempe operator's distraction to her company's safety culture and the state's oversight and addressed its recommendations to them, so blame is one carrier of upstream provenance and not its only source *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-755](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-755.md) — Dynamical separation of time scales (fast deviations relax, leaving a slow collective variable) and economic separation (costly formation, cheap repeated use) are different and come apart both ways: a slow variable can save no work, and a result reused cheaply need not be an attractor of any dynamics; so amortization is not in general a separation of time scales in the sense of the owner's scale-separation claim, and a constraint that is both is a further fact *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-121](../record/arguments.d/ARG-121.md) — The three-arm case's slow register that no member reads, and its rule passed through an archive between episodes that never run together, show that dynamical and economic separation of time scales come apart in both directions *(Proposed, existence)*
- [CLAIM-756](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-756.md) — An acquisition can be worth making for what it does to the cost of other acquisitions: valued only by its own savings on a fixed task distribution, a learning step that lowers the cost of a later one can show a loss, and the ranking of learning policies can reverse once its effect on later acquisitions is counted *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-766](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-766.md) — In children's equal division of jointly earned spoils, the joint "we" supplies the motive to settle the division and the equal split supplies its content as the conspicuous solution the situation affords, so the obligation reading and the coordination reading are complementary, and at age three the conspicuous split is a known default rather than a focal point found by mutual expectation *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-772](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-772.md) — Forgetting a source and anchoring to it are one contraction, told apart by what each restatement step conserves exactly: a chain that contracts everywhere except on what its steps copy without error ends keeping exactly the start's value on that conserved part, so it is anchored where the source's features lie in the part and forgets them where they do not; the record copies content exactly, by code and verbatim reading, and leaves form to contract onto its schema *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-795](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-795.md) — Power laws arise from many mechanisms with no positive feedback: a branching process balanced between extinction and growth, a tuned critical point, first-passage times of a random walk, a mixture of exponential rates, sample-space reduction, steady growth with a spread of ages, and an inverse power of a uniform variable *(Proposed, thesis)*

  - [ARG-176](../record/arguments.d/ARG-176.md) — Reed and Hughes's deterministic case, as a source, carries item 6 of the catalogue of feedback-free power-law mechanisms as stated, while their double Pareto for noisy growth shows the item's ratio of rates to be the noise-free limit *(Proposed, source)*

- [CLAIM-798](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-798.md) — Reading a network's representations as active matter splits into a weak analogy, that embeddings move collectively under optimization and noise through a shared-parameter kernel, and a strong model, that their dynamics carry sustained nonequilibrium currents or persistent orientation-like degrees of freedom not reducible to gradient relaxation; the weak reading follows from gradient flow, the strong one has to be shown, and its flocking observable is alignment of velocities, not clustering of positions *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-126](../record/arguments.d/ARG-126.md) — The Lyapunov identity for embeddings coupled through a shared-parameter kernel closes the feedback loop between kernel and representation as a route to active dynamics, so the strong active-matter reading needs a source outside gradient flow *(Proposed, formal-application)*

- [CLAIM-799](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-799.md) — Geometric separation, decodability and spectral detectability are distinct qualities of a learned representation that need not agree: a semantic direction can be decodable while related points are almost orthogonal, and a covariance spike yields a PCA outlier only above the BBP threshold √(D/N), which marks when that estimator can see the signal, not when the network acquired it *(Proposed, thesis)*

  - [ARG-171](../record/arguments.d/ARG-171.md) — Park and colleagues' solvable teacher–student model, as an existence case, shows that the signal can be in the weights while the weight spectrum has no outlier, so the outlier's appearance marks spectral visibility and not acquisition, as the separation of qualities says, against the paper's own reading of the outlier as the emergence of representations *(Proposed, existence)*

- [CLAIM-800](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-800.md) — Occupancy of entailment cones is not a measure of learning: it rises when cone boundaries move as well as when representations flow, it rises under collapse, and nested cones make a coarse concept's cone entered no later than a fine one's by construction, so coarse-to-fine learning needs an independent measure of when each level's distinction becomes decodable *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-801](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-801.md) — Sloppy-model behaviour, behavioural complexity set by a few combinations of many parameters, probably does carry over to overparameterized neural networks, by a route other than the analogy from regular Fisher spectra *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-803](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-803.md) — A power-law distribution does not identify the mechanism that produced it, nor does a shared power law show a shared mechanism or universality class; the mechanism has to be read from the dynamics, whether gain scales with size, whether there are floors or resets, whether the cutoff grows with the system, after the tail has been fitted against alternatives such as the lognormal *(Proposed, thesis)*

  - [ARG-170](../record/arguments.d/ARG-170.md) — Broido and Clauset's test of 928 network degree distributions, as a source, supports for network degrees that a power law is weak evidence of its mechanism and that the tail must be fitted against the lognormal first, while naming no dynamical test *(Proposed, source)*

- [CLAIM-804](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-804.md) — If learned signal strengths fall as a power law in rank, the number of directions PCA can separate from the noise bulk grows as a power of the sample-to-dimension ratio and of the signal gain, a cascade of detectability thresholds and not a self-organized critical process, and the power law then belongs to the hierarchy of signal strengths, not to the spectrum, whose bulk with a few outliers is no heavy tail *(Proposed, supposed)*
  - [ARG-145](../record/arguments.d/ARG-145.md) — Baik, Ben Arous and Péché prove the spiked threshold only for the largest eigenvalue of complex Gaussian samples with at least as many samples as variables, so for claims about real data, eigenvectors or several outliers their paper corroborates and does not ground *(Proposed, source)*
  - [ARG-151](../record/arguments.d/ARG-151.md) — Baik and Silverstein's almost-sure limits carry the spiked threshold and outlier location to real samples, to more variables than samples, and to each of finitely many spikes, as the claims that apply them need *(Proposed, formal-application)*
- [CLAIM-805](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-805.md) — Entropy, correlation and scaling are distinct properties of a system, and a critical point is not the maximum of complexity: what is special there is the absence of a finite correlation scale, while entropy density, predictive information, the number of relevant directions and the cost of simulation need not peak there *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-806](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-806.md) — Linear preferential attachment is itself balanced at a boundary, between the stretched-exponential tails of weaker attachment and the condensation of stronger, so rich-get-richer processes and criticality are not opposite routes to a power law: both reach one at a marginal point, and differ in what is balanced *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-807](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-807.md) — A factored feature under weight decay, ŷ = abφ, switches on at a sharp threshold: its strength is q* = (s − λ)₊, the origin loses stability through a pitchfork in the parameters at s = λ, relaxation there is algebraic and the local coefficient of the regularized loss dips from 1 to 3/4, and just above threshold the feature's variance is of order ε² while its gain in fit is of order ε, so a newly active feature is quiet but consequential *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-809](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-809.md) — Nearness to a dynamical transition changes what a system computes well rather than raising every computational ability: memory and separation, sensitivity, reliability and speed pull apart, total capacity is bounded by the number of independent state variables, and the best distance from the transition depends on the task, the integration window and the correlations of the environment *(Proposed, thesis)*

  - [ARG-148](../record/arguments.d/ARG-148.md) — The scalar linear reservoir is an exactly solved instance of nearness to a transition redistributing a bounded computational capacity rather than raising it, though not by the memory-noise tradeoff the exchange gives *(Proposed, existence)*
  - [ARG-163](../record/arguments.d/ARG-163.md) — Azizpour and colleagues' branching network with a finite-time leaky readout, as evidence, supports the claim that the best distance from a dynamical transition depends on the integration window and the task, for one transition and one task family *(Proposed, evidence)*
  - [ARG-196](../record/arguments.d/ARG-196.md) — Natschläger, Bertschinger and Legenstein's driven threshold networks, whose readout does best near the order-to-chaos line when averaged over many tasks, as evidence, support the claim's memory-against-separation strand and leave its thesis standing, since a task-averaged optimum with no per-task optima does not meet its defeater *(Proposed, evidence)*

- [CLAIM-810](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-810.md) — Scale invariance, dependence across scales and transfer across scales are three properties, any of which can occur without the others, so a hierarchy of structure is not a hierarchy of causation *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-811](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-811.md) — Gradient flow into a degenerate minimum relaxes algebraically, not exponentially, and how slowly is not fixed by the learning coefficient: on the balanced line of a k-fold product loss the decay is t^(−1/(2k−2)) while the real log canonical threshold stays ½ and only its multiplicity grows to k *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-157](../record/arguments.d/ARG-157.md) — Wei and colleagues' first integral of the averaged gradient flow near an overlap singularity, read as grounds, shows that gradient flow into a degenerate minimum relaxes algebraically and that slow, power-law-like relaxation in training may be such relaxation *(Rejected, evidence)*

- [CLAIM-812](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-812.md) — Sloppiness and singular strata meet in two places and part in one: a sloppy eigenvalue near a stratum measures the squared distance to it, and at a finite sample size a direction too sloppy to resolve contributes to the learning coefficient no more than a flat one; they part in how the coefficient moves with sample size, rising about ½ for each direction resolved in a regular sloppy model toward d/2, and held below d/2 at every size in a singular one *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-813](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-813.md) — Sloppiness and singularity are different properties of a statistical model: sloppiness is a spread of small but nonzero Fisher eigenvalues in a regular model, singularity is rank loss on a stratum of parameter space, so a model can be sloppy everywhere and singular nowhere or singular everywhere with no spread, and at a singular point the Fisher spectrum does not give the learning coefficient *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-133](../record/arguments.d/ARG-133.md) — Transtrum, Machta and Sethna's geometry supports the claim that sloppiness and singularity are different properties: the singular points of a sloppy manifold's metric lie mostly at infinite parameter values and at finite fold lines only in some models, though the two meet at the manifold's edges *(Proposed, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-814](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-814.md) — In the scalar linear reservoir x(t+1) = a x(t) + u(t) + η(t), the gain a does not trade memory against noise: the state's signal-to-noise ratio and its total linear memory capacity s²/(s²+σ²) do not depend on a, which only spreads that capacity over lags; recalling the input k steps back is best at a = √(k/(k+1)), and noise added at the readout makes capacity rise monotonically toward a = 1 *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-815](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-815.md) — The exponent 3/2 shared by critical branching cascades and first passage of a random walk comes from one identity, the hitting-time theorem: the chance of total size s, or of first passage at time t, is 1/s or 1/t times a local probability that falls as the inverse square root at balance, so 3/2 = 1 + 1/2 *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-817](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-817.md) — Cumulative advantage gives a power law only in a particular form: attachment linear in current size together with continual entry of new units; with no preference the tail is exponential, with sublinear preference stretched-exponential, and with superlinear preference one unit takes almost every new link *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-820](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-820.md) — A model's parameter complexity and its behavioural complexity come apart: when its predictions depend on a few stiff combinations of parameters and barely on the rest, it can be hard to fit and still predictive, so simplicity can belong to how a system responds to observation rather than to its mechanism *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-823](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-823.md) — Alternative reading (b) of the owner's suggestion on singularities: a phase transition in learning is a change in which singular region of parameter space dominates, as the sample size grows, between regions that fit differently and have different learning coefficients, and resolution of singularities is the tool that computes those coefficients *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-824](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-824.md) — Multiplicative growth with independent, identically distributed returns gives a lognormal cross-section, not a power law, but the same growth with an additive floor gives a stationary power-law tail whose exponent κ solves E[A^κ] = 1, a condition that requires the process to contract on average in logarithm *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-825](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-825.md) — A model has no single practical dimension: the number of parameter directions a data set resolves grows with the data, as a power of the sample size when the Fisher spectrum falls as a power of rank and as its logarithm when it falls exponentially, so zooming out and demanding precision move effective dimension in opposite directions *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-827](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-827.md) — The occupancy threshold of a cone holding a fixed share of random directions, the BBP threshold and the alignment bifurcation are three different thresholds on one scale of alignment strength: the first at κ of order √D, the second at κ = √D·(D/N)^(1/4), the third at a coupling of order D; only the last is a transition of the system, and in the mean-field alignment model the ordering mode becomes BBP-detectable at coupling D/(1 + √(D/N)), an early warning before the bifurcation at D *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-829](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-829.md) — Read as a separation of scales, a bulk separated from a sparse tail is what a continuous transition shows from below: the bulk keeps a fixed small scale while the cutoff of the tail grows without bound as the transition nears, and at the transition the separating scale is gone, so that no size marks off the extraordinary *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-830](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-830.md) — The mean-field derivation of the Barabási–Albert power law is the age mechanism in logarithmic time, so what separates linear preferential attachment from Gibrat's lognormal growth is the continual entry of new units and not the proportionality of growth *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-833](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-833.md) — Model reduction and feature differentiation may be movements in opposite directions through one stratified space of effective models: reduction moves toward the boundaries of the model manifold, where parameters stop mattering, and differentiation moves away from singular strata, where redundant features become separately usable *(Proposed, supposed)*

- [CLAIM-835](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-835.md) — Whether a direction in a learned model is small depends on the metric it is measured in, and the metrics can rank directions in opposite orders: a label can sit wholly in the least-variance component, and the predictive Fisher pulled back to a hidden state, Wᵀ(diag p − ppᵀ)W, can rank a weight matrix's smallest singular direction above its largest *(Proposed, thesis)*

  - [ARG-151](../record/arguments.d/ARG-151.md) — Baik and Silverstein's almost-sure limits carry the spiked threshold and outlier location to real samples, to more variables than samples, and to each of finitely many spikes, as the claims that apply them need *(Proposed, formal-application)*
- [CLAIM-839](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-839.md) — Progressive learning can be described by two partial orders, semantic entailment among the regions a representation assigns and informational refinement among its checkpoints in Blackwell's sense, neither of which need be a chain: learning is then the construction of an increasingly informative branching order of distinctions, and a narrower region counts as progress only while it stays correct *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-841](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-841.md) — A power law or a scale-invariant law does not by itself indicate criticality: symmetry, flux, growth, coarsening, geometry and broad relaxation spectra each remove a characteristic scale without a tuned transition *(Proposed, thesis)*

  - [ARG-181](../record/arguments.d/ARG-181.md) — The record's simulation of the two-dimensional sandpile, as evidence, corroborates the claim that a power law does not by itself indicate criticality in its granted bullet that self-organized criticality reaches a critical point without tuning, since the cutoff grows with lattice size and no parameter was set *(Proposed, evidence)*

- [CLAIM-842](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-842.md) — If a representation's collective deformations have a local Gaussian elastic energy on an interaction graph of spectral dimension d_s, their long-wavelength fluctuations diverge for d_s at or below 2, so whether conventional order survives is set by the spectral dimension of the interaction geometry, not by layer width *(Proposed, supposed)*
  - [ARG-200](../record/arguments.d/ARG-200.md) — Gelfert and Nolting's report of Cassi's theorem, with Nachtergaele's proof and Halperin's limits, read as sources, shows that the spectral-dimension criterion of the claim about a representation's long-wavelength fluctuations is a theorem for spin models with a continuous symmetry in equilibrium, not Mermin and Wagner's own result, and holds only under conditions a trained representation is not shown to meet *(Proposed, source)*
- [CLAIM-844](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-844.md) — Some of the slow, power-law-like relaxation seen in training deep networks may be the algebraic relaxation of degenerate singular modes rather than critical slowing down in a collective phase, and a dependency tree of feature transitions yields power laws only if its thresholds or relaxation times are themselves broadly or self-similarly distributed *(Proposed, thesis)*

  - [ARG-157](../record/arguments.d/ARG-157.md) — Wei and colleagues' first integral of the averaged gradient flow near an overlap singularity, read as grounds, shows that gradient flow into a degenerate minimum relaxes algebraically and that slow, power-law-like relaxation in training may be such relaxation *(Rejected, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-845](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-845.md) — Read as a gap in support, a bulk separated from a sparse tail is not what a continuous transition shows from below, where the size distribution falls without a break into an exponential cutoff; a bulk beside a separate population of large sizes belongs to the far side of the transition, as a giant cluster or a major outbreak in a finite system, or to a first-order transition *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-847](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-847.md) — For a Gaussian representation the relative spread of the squared norm is √(2/D_PR), with D_PR the covariance participation ratio, so concentration is set by effective rather than ambient dimension; under a rank power-law spectrum λ_j ∝ j^−α, D_PR grows as D for α below 1/2, as D/log D at 1/2, as D^(2(1−α)) between 1/2 and 1, as (log D)² at 1, and tends to a constant above 1 *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-130](../record/arguments.d/ARG-130.md) — The finite-width computation for a rank power-law spectrum supports the participation-ratio regimes as asymptotic statements and qualifies their use: just either side of an exponent of 1 they separate only at widths no network has, so they cannot be read from width scaling *(Proposed, formal-application)*
- [CLAIM-848](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-848.md) — A rank power-law spectrum with exponent just above 1, at the limit that Stringer's smoothness bound, α > 1 + 2/m on the tail of a smooth code of an m-dimensional stimulus manifold, allows, bounds the participation ratio as width grows, but the bound is approached only at widths exponential in m, so at realistic widths such a code has a participation ratio of about 13 to 29 for m from 10 to 100, and neither the participation ratio nor its growth with width tracks intrinsic dimension or separates the regimes either side of α = 1 *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-849](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-849.md) — When past and future are independent given a shared parameter, the shape of the Fisher spectrum fixes how predictive information grows: in a linear-Gaussian model it grows as (d/2) ln T with d resolved directions, as T^(1/p) when the spectrum falls as j^(−p), and as (ln T)²/(4a) when it falls as e^(−aj), so the power-law regime of Bialek, Nemenman and Tishby follows from a power-law spectrum *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-154](../record/arguments.d/ARG-154.md) — Bialek, Nemenman and Tishby ground the logarithmic case of the claim that the Fisher spectrum's shape fixes how predictive information grows, and its power-law case as to exponent only, as an instance of their annealed result; its exponential-spectrum case is not in their paper *(Proposed, evidence)*
- [CLAIM-850](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-850.md) — Chaos, criticality and a cascade through scales are distinct properties, and each can occur without either of the others; they meet only through particular mechanisms, such as the period-doubling accumulation point, which is critical in the renormalization-group sense and not chaotic *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-852](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-852.md) — The sign flip that Acharya, Rimal and Dhakal call the dual geometry of transformer representations is what Park, Choe and Veitch's map from unembedding to embedding representations predicts: the map multiplies a concept's unembedding contrast by the inverse of the unembedding covariance, which divides each eigencomponent by its eigenvalue and so moves the vector's energy toward the spectral tail, a rescaling in a fixed eigenbasis rather than a rotation of concept information by the forward pass *(Proposed, thesis)*

- [CLAIM-854](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-854.md) — The most informative signal in a learned spectrum lies in a truncated band: the top directions carry common, weakly discriminating structure, as stop words do in a corpus, the extreme bottom carries low-signal outliers, as rare words do, and once both are cut, the bottom of the retained band holds the most discriminating directions *(Proposed, thesis)*
