- [CLAIM-855](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-855.md) — An alternative to the stop-word half of the owner's truncated-band account: top spectral directions that track the data's leading principal components, its common high-variance structure, may be a mark of under-trained or large-step regimes that learning reorganizes away from, rather than a standing feature of a learned spectrum *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-174](../record/arguments.d/ARG-174.md) — Park and colleagues' Fig. 16, by analogy from an MLP regressor's first-layer weights to a language model's unembedding, suggests that top directions tracking the data's common high-variance structure belong to large-step or under-trained regimes, a rival to the stop-word half of the truncated-band account *(Proposed, analogy)*
- [CLAIM-856](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-856.md) — An alternative to the floor and band of the owner's truncated-band account: the fine end of a learned spectrum may be damped for smoothness and generalization, with discrimination growing steadily toward it, and the floor a measurement finds below it may be estimator noise rather than a class of low-signal outliers bounding a band of highly discriminating directions *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-173](../record/arguments.d/ARG-173.md) — Stringer and colleagues' smoothing account of spectral decay, by analogy from a sensory population code to a learned spectrum, suggests that the fine end is damped for generalization and that the measured floor is estimator noise, a rival to the floor and band of the truncated-band account *(Proposed, analogy)*
- [CLAIM-908](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-908.md) — The matched constructions proposed for testing contractualism, as stated, are each explained by reasonable rejection without a principle of who holds a power: a principle permitting the worse member of each pair can be reasonably rejected on personal reasons of protection, against undetectable error, self-serving review, engineered dependence and unilateral change, so as stated they support the reading on which the record's account only supplements contractualism *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-203](../record/arguments.d/ARG-203.md) — Applying reasonable rejection, as the SEP entry states it, to the four matched constructions on one courier platform, each pair's worse member is disallowed by protective personal reasons alone, so the constructions as stated are explained without a principle of who holds a power *(Proposed, formal-application)*
- [CLAIM-949](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-949.md) — The record's account of specification is model-theoretic, a set of tests and the versions that pass them all, as an institution pairs sentences with the models that satisfy them; type theory is its proof-relevant counterpart, in which a specification is a type, a question a problem, a realization an inhabitant carried with the evidence that it passes, adding a descriptor a refinement the entry provably inhabits, which is why descriptors cannot conflict, and the direction of fit is bidirectional typing's split between inferring a type from a term and checking a term against a type given *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-208](../record/arguments.d/ARG-208.md) — Freeman and Pfenning's split between inferred refinements and annotations checked against them, by analogy, shows that the direction of fit is the split between inferring a type from a term and checking a term against a type given *(Rejected, analogy)*
  - [ARG-209](../record/arguments.d/ARG-209.md) — Freeman and Pfenning's refinement types, by analogy, show that adding a descriptor is refining a type its entry already inhabits, and that descriptors cannot conflict because the entry inhabits their intersection *(Proposed, analogy)*
  - [ARG-211](../record/arguments.d/ARG-211.md) — Davies and Pfenning's checking judgment, which takes its type from the programmer's ascription and passes it down to subterms, by analogy, shows that checking holds a term to a type given in advance, world to word, as against synthesis *(Proposed, analogy)*
  - [ARG-212](../record/arguments.d/ARG-212.md) — Davies and Pfenning's bidirectional refinement checking, by analogy, shows that the move that fits a term to a type it is checked against is elaboration or coercion *(Rejected, analogy)*
  - [ARG-213](../record/arguments.d/ARG-213.md) — Liquid type inference, and the checking of liquid programs against types given in advance, by analogy, show that the direction of fit is the split between inferring a type from a term and checking a term against a type given *(Rejected, analogy)*
  - [ARG-214](../record/arguments.d/ARG-214.md) — Liquid types' refinements {ν : B | φ}, by analogy, show that adding a descriptor is refining, by a predicate, a type its entry already inhabits, and that the descriptors that can be found mechanically are conjunctions from a vocabulary fixed in advance *(Proposed, analogy)*
- [CLAIM-960](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-960.md) — For a whole that is a bare relational arrangement, being a constituent adds no obligation beyond those grounded in the constituent's vulnerability, interests, rights and exposure to power: the part-whole relation locates where an obligation applies without grounding it, and because such an arrangement is not an agent the obligation falls on the agents or roles that maintain, control or benefit from it, not on the whole *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-207](../record/arguments.d/ARG-207.md) — The matched member and non-member pair of the part-whole case, by contrast, together with a bare relational arrangement's not being an agent, shows that for such a whole constitution grounds no further obligation and that the bearer is the controlling agents, not the whole *(Proposed, contrast)*
- [CLAIM-983](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-983.md) — In the transmission criterion of identity over time, a maintainer that restores an individual from the organization it finds in it is a channel of transmission, never part of what is transmitted, so replacing the maintainer with an unrelated one breaks no continuation and the criterion is met or failed by the path through the individual itself *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-216](../record/arguments.d/ARG-216.md) — A collective whose members are all replaced continues because each newcomer takes its organization from the collective as found, and an unrelated maintainer restores a thing from the organization it finds in the thing, so by analogy replacing a maintainer leaves a causal path from the earlier relations to the later through the thing, and a car that changes garages is a continuation, not the defeater of the transmission criterion *(Proposed, analogy)*
- [CLAIM-986](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-986.md) — In the transmission criterion of identity over time, an outside maintainer's organization is part of what is transmitted just insofar as it holds organization the repertoire depends on that the individual does not carry and that a competent unrelated replacement, working from the individual, would not supply; a garage holds none of a car's, so a change of garage continues the car whole, while an unrelated new maintainer can continue a project only in the respects its code carries *(Proposed, thesis)*
  - [ARG-216](../record/arguments.d/ARG-216.md) — A collective whose members are all replaced continues because each newcomer takes its organization from the collective as found, and an unrelated maintainer restores a thing from the organization it finds in the thing, so by analogy replacing a maintainer leaves a causal path from the earlier relations to the later through the thing, and a car that changes garages is a continuation, not the defeater of the transmission criterion *(Proposed, analogy)*
- [CLAIM-987](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-987.md) — Alternative reading (a) of the constitutivism test: applied to the record's organizational account, Leffler's choice point cannot be passed from an organization's dynamics alone, since if the force of its self-generated norms is explained by its being continuously positioned to maintain itself, that force is relative to its constitution, and the account cannot by that route rule between an institution's norms and its members' without a premise from outside the dynamics *(Proposed, counter)*
  - [ARG-217](../record/arguments.d/ARG-217.md) — Leffler's plight-inescapability argument, carried by analogy from agents to self-maintaining organizations, shows that a constitutive explanation of the force of an organization's norms makes that force relative to the organization's constitution *(Proposed, analogy)*
